root_cause: The prior stages intentionally stopped at provider-neutral dispatch and injected publication Protocols. That preserved authority boundaries but left the final effect boundary to each embedding application. There is no repository-owned structured workspace mutation adapter, real local Git host, GitHub PR-create host, or fail-closed bootstrap that assembles them for an installed Starter.
causal_chain: CapabilityResolver binds workspace.write, vcs.commit.create, and code_review.pull_request.create to provider identities.
WorkflowAdapterDispatcher enforces WriteAuthorityGuard before calling a mutating Provider Adapter.
local.workspace has no executable adapter at all.
LocalGitProviderAdapter and CodeReviewProviderAdapter validate receipts but delegate effects to Protocols.
All repository tests for those hosts use in-memory fakes, so no real Git repository or remote exact-head response is proved.
StarterWorkflowRuntime accepts a ProviderAdapterRegistry but exposes no canonical concrete assembly, so embeddings must duplicate security-sensitive setup.
rejected_hypotheses: Put Git or GitHub commands inside Customer Agent Skills; this would couple methodology to providers and bypass capability dispatch.
Treat fake host receipts as concrete integration evidence; they prove shape validation only.
Grant write permission from composition or provider availability; binding is not authority.
Let the GitHub host merge after CI; Customer Agent publication Workflows intentionally stop after CI and contain no merge capability.
Execute arbitrary shell or project command text from Workflow state; runtime effects require closed structured contracts.
affected_boundaries: GitHub repository and PR exact-head identity
